'''Jemerrio Jones''' (born April 9, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Santos del Potosí]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State Aggies]].

==College career==
Jones began focusing on rebounding at a young age growing up in [[Memphis, Tennessee]]. He tore his ACL as a junior in high school and this limited his college options. Jones ended up at [[Hill College]] and averaged 11.7 points per game over two seasons. He broke the NJCAA tournament rebounding record with 72 rebounds in five games. He committed to play at New Mexico State.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fuchs|first1=Jeremy|title=New Mexico State's 6'5" Senior Jemerrio Jones Is A Rebounding Machine|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/02/jemerrio-jones-new-mexico-state-rebounder-senior-ncaa-tournament|access-date=March 30, 2018|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=March 2, 2018}}</ref>

He was named the 2017–18 [[Western Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|WAC Player of the Year]].

As a senior, Jones became the first player since 1997 to record 20+ rebounds in three straight games.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Varlas|first1=John|title=Sunday Sports Brunch: Perseverance pays off for Jemerrio Jones|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/2018/02/18/sunday-sports-brunch-perseverance-pays-off-jemerrio-jones/326748002/|access-date=March 30, 2018|work=The Commercial-Appeal|date=February 18, 2018}}</ref> He averaged 11.0 points, 13.2 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game in his senior year. He was named WAC Tournament Most Valuable Player since he averaged 12.3 points and 18.3 rebounds per game over three tournament games. Jones set a WAC single-season record with 450 rebounds and was named WAC Player of the Year. He was also named to the National Association of Basketball Coaches (NABC) All-District 6 first team and to the US Basketball Writers Association (USBWA) All-District VIII Team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Aggie Jones named AP honorable mention All-American|url=https://www.abqjournal.com/1151289/aggie-jones-named-ap-honorable-mention-all-american.html|access-date=March 30, 2018|work=[[Albuquerque Journal]]|date=March 27, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===South Bay Lakers (2018–2019)===
After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Jones was selected with the 18th pick of the [[2018 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]]. Shortly thereafter, he was traded alongside a 2019 first-round pick to the [[South Bay Lakers]] for the rights to Serbian player [[Alen Smailagić]].<ref>{{cite news|title=G League Draft: Santa Cruz Warriors select Jordan Howard, make 2 draft-day trades|url=https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/2018/10/20/g-league-draft-santa-cruz-warriors-select-jordan-howard-make-2-draft-day-trades/|work=[[Santa Cruz Sentinel]]|date=October 20, 2018|access-date=October 22, 2018}}</ref> He was added to the training camp roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=South Bay finalizes training camp roster and schedule|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-finalizes-training-camp-roster-and-schedule/|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2018|access-date=October 23, 2018|archive-date=October 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181023200436/https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-finalizes-training-camp-roster-and-schedule/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2019)===
On March 31, 2019, Jones signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Jemerrio Jones|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/190331sign-jemerrio-jones|website=NBA.com|date=March 31, 2019|access-date=March 31, 2019}}</ref> In his NBA debut, Jones had two points, one rebound and one steal against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Lakers' Jemerrio Jones: Makes NBA debut|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/lakers-jemerrio-jones-makes-nba-debut/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=April 1, 2019|access-date=May 12, 2020}}</ref> On April 7, Jones started for the Lakers, grabbing a career-high 16 rebounds in a 113–109 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz vs Los Angeles Lakers – Box Score|url=https://www.nba.com/game/uta-vs-lal-0021801208/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|date=April 7, 2019|access-date=December 21, 2021}}</ref>

===Wisconsin Herd (2019–2020)===
On July 5, 2019, Jones was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in a three-team trade.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-wagner-bonga-jones-lakers-trade|title=Wizards acquire Wagner, Jones and Bonga from Lakers|work=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2019|access-date=July 5, 2019}}</ref> On October 16, 2019, Jones was waived by the Wizards after the team's four preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|first=Candace|last=Buckner|title=Wizards make roster moves, waive veteran Justin Anderson|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/10/16/wizards-make-roster-moves-waive-veteran-justin-anderson/|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=October 17, 2019|access-date=October 17, 2019}}</ref>

Jones joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]] of the [[NBA G League]] after being acquired in a trade.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jerell|last=Rushkin|title=New-look Wisconsin Herd opens NBA G League season at home|url=https://www.thenorthwestern.com/story/sports/2019/11/07/nba-g-league-new-look-wisconsin-herd-opens-season-menominee-nation-arena-oshkosh/2506861001/|work=[[Oshkosh Northwestern]]|date=November 7, 2019|access-date=November 26, 2019}}</ref> He was suspended a game against the [[Erie BayHawks (2019–)|Erie BayHawks]] on March 9, 2020, for compiling his 13th technical foul. In the 2019–20 season, Jones averaged 10.8 points, 12.0 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.3 steals per game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jemerrio Jones: Suspended against Erie|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jemerrio-jones-suspended-against-erie/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=May 12, 2020}}</ref>

===Delaware Blue Coats (2021)===
Jones joined the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] for their 2021 restart, making his debut in their season opener on February 11, 2021.<ref>{{cite news|title=DELAWARE BLUE COATS SELECT JEMERRIO JONES AND BRAXTON KEY IN 2021 NBA G LEAGUE DRAFT|url=https://www.witn22.org/2021/01/12/delaware-blue-coats-select-jemerrio-jones-and-braxton-key-in-2021-nba-g-league-draft/|work=WITN22|date=January 12, 2021|access-date=October 31, 2021}}</ref>

===Return to Wisconsin (2021)===
In October 2021, Jones rejoined the [[Wisconsin Herd]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wisconsin Herd Announces 2021 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announces-2021-training-camp-roster/n-5758540|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 26, 2021|access-date=October 30, 2021}}</ref> In 11 games, he averaged 6.5 points, 8.3 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.5 steals in 25.7 minutes per game.<ref name="LAL202110d">{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Jemerrio Jones to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-jemerrio-jones-10-day-contract-2021|website=NBA.com|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}}</ref>

===Return to Los Angeles (2021)===
On December 21, 2021, Jones returned to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] after signing a 10-day contract.<ref name="LAL202110d" />

===Third stint with Wisconsin (2021–2022)===
On December 31, 2021, Jones was reacquired by the [[Wisconsin Herd]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=December 31, 2021|access-date=December 31, 2021}}</ref>

===Return to South Bay (2022)===
On February 2, 2022, Jones was traded to the [[South Bay Lakers]] in exchange for the returning player rights to [[Wayne Selden Jr.|Wayne Selden]], a 2022 first-round draft pick, and a 2022 third-round draft pick.<ref>{{Cite web|title=South Bay Lakers Acquire Jemerrio Jones in Trade with Wisconsin|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-jemerrio-jones-in-trade-with-wisconsin/|access-date=February 6, 2022|website=NBA G League}}</ref>

===Lakeland / Osceola Magic (2022–2025)===
On November 3, 2022, Jones was named to the opening night roster for the [[Osceola Magic|Lakeland Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakeland Magic Announce 2022–23 Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/lakeland-magic-announce-2022-23-opening-night-roster/n-5895510|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}}</ref>

On October 27, 2024, Jones joined the [[Osceola Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Osceola Magic Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/osceola-magic-announce-training-camp-roster/n-6160339|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}}</ref> However, he was waived on January 15, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=OSCEOLA MAGIC ACQUIRE COLIN CASTLETON FROM LONG ISLAND NETS|url=https://osceola.gleague.nba.com/news/osceola-magic-acquire-colin-castleton-from-long-island-nets|website=NBA.com|date=January 15, 2025|access-date=January 15, 2025}}</ref>
